content.comment_body: Hello, does the [product_name] module offer built-in debouncing for its inputs? The user manual doesn’t mention it, so I assume it’s not included. Also, how often can the [product_name] update the memory cells related to input states? According to the manual, regular digital inputs support a maximum frequency of 4 Hz, which means inputs can change only every 0.25 seconds, even though the program cycle is shorter. For instance, the [article_no] module lacks fast inputs, so its digital inputs appear to update every 0.25 seconds. Is this accurate?
Apologies, English is not my first language. Could you clarify what bounce protection means?

To clarify, "debouncing" refers to filtering out unwanted noise from buttons or switches, preventing accidental multiple activations. This technique is commonly used in hardware and software to ensure consistent input detection.
It appears that digital inputs on the [product_name] module are not inherently debounced. For an official response from [company_name], consider submitting a support request.

Because the scan rate of [product_name] (four times per second) is relatively slow, it effectively serves as a debouncing measure. You can connect a digital input with a physical push button to a relay function block trigger input and expect reliable performance.

Hi, I’ve used an inexpensive toggle switch for testing. When switching slowly, there was no noticeable bounce, but rapid switching sometimes produced multiple pulses. I directly connected counters to the inputs and measured switching frequencies up to 5 kHz. This approach can reveal whether the switch shows bounce effects. This was done for experimental purposes.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are discussing whether the [product_name] digital inputs have built-in debouncing and how quickly the module registers input changes. There is some ambiguity due to the lack of clear information in official documents about debounce functionality. Users point out that the module’s lower scan rate minimizes bounce problems under normal conditions, but very rapid input changes can still produce unwanted signals.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for explicit confirmation about debouncing features in the [product_name] module and seek details on how often its digital inputs are updated. Their goal is to have reliable input detection without false activations from electrical noise or switch bounce.
